fatal_errors: The proposed high-temperature brazing intervention is fundamentally different from the target liquid-metal dealloying process.
The hypothesis omits selective dissolution of Ti-rich interdendritic regions and their replacement by molten Cu.
It incorrectly identifies an added refractory filler alloy as the structural mediator rather than the bicontinuous RHEA-ligament/Cu-channel architecture and spontaneously formed W-rich interlayer.
The stated processing time, pressure, and solid-state starting configuration are unsupported and conflict with immersion in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h in a vacuum-sealed silica enclosure.
The predicted 20–30% bond-strength improvement and residual-stress reduction are invented; interfacial bond strength was not the principal measured outcome.
No supporting evidence is cited for the filler-alloy mechanism or quantitative outcome.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad challenge of joining an RHEA with Cu at high temperature, but it does not reconstruct the reported method or findings. The target used liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor, exploiting preferential Ti–Cu exchange to form aligned Cu channels, retained BCC RHEA ligaments, and a passivating W-rich interlayer. The generated hypothesis instead proposes conventional brazing with an unspecified filler and unsupported interdiffusion and bond-strength claims. Its comparative brazing experiment is testable, but it would evaluate a different, unevidenced materials strategy and would not discriminate the target mechanism or reproduce the thermal-conductivity and helium-irradiation results.
